history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: Bhismaknagar is a fortified archaeological settlement (part of the Chutia kingdom's Sadhayapura capital region, identified with the fortified hill city of Doi-Thang in the Buranjis), not a temple. Excavations exposed earthen ramparts, brick gateways, plinths, tanks and a large brick-built central complex (1,860 sq m plinth, three halls, extension rooms, six entrances) yielding terracotta plaques, figurines, decorative tiles and inscribed bricks; the name derives from the Bhismak legend popularised via 16th-century Vaishnavite traditions (earlier colonial accounts applied the name to a different site). DATE CONFLICT (verify): Wikipedia infobox says built 8th century/abandoned 16th century; roing.nic.in dates it tentatively to the 8th century; its tourist circuit page says circa 12th century AD; another travel source says 1100 CE; the site article dates the ruins 11th-16th centuries.

name: Bhismaknagar Fort
town_description: Roing is the headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley district in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Dibang river. It is the gateway town for the Dibang Valley circuit, Bhismaknagar ruins, Mehao Lake and Mayudia, and lies at about 28.14N 95.84E at roughly 800 m elevation.
tradition: Archaeological site (Chutia fortified settlement; not a temple)

travel.airport: Dibrugarh Airport (Assam), about 100-120 km; Tezu Airport (TEI) has limited scheduled flights.
travel.railway: Tinsukia Junction (Assam), about 90-100 km away, is the nearest major railhead.
travel.road: About 29 km south-east of Roing on plateau-like foothill terrain; approachable by road via Koronu village.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April; avoid the monsoon months (June-September) when foothill roads can be affected.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open archaeological site with no fixed hours; visit in daylight (verify locally).
